name: New Look
summary: The couture line that Christian Dior showed in February 1947. It has round shoulders, a small built waist and a full calf-length skirt in metres of wool and silk. It answered the rationed, square dress of the war.

philosophy.core_thesis: After rationing, a woman's dress shows plenty: a small waist, a full skirt and the hand work of the couture house.
design_principles: Cut the waist 5 to 8 cm smaller than the natural waist, and hold it with a boned inner belt.
Set the hem 30 to 40 cm above the floor, at mid-calf.
Give a day skirt a hem of 10 to 25 m, and an evening skirt up to 80 m.
Round the shoulder with no pad; let the line run down from the neck in one curve.
Pad the hip with a basque so that the waist looks smaller.
Build the shape inside the dress with canvas, boning and a tulle petticoat.
Finish each seam and each hem by hand.
anti_patterns: Square padded shoulders of wartime utility dress
Short straight skirts that save cloth
Thin, limp cloth that cannot hold a pleat
Visible machine top-stitching on a couture piece

silhouette.shape: An hourglass: a fitted bodice, a small waist and a skirt that stands out in a wide bell or falls in a narrow pencil.
silhouette.line: A soft round shoulder, a waist at the natural line, and a hem at mid-calf.
silhouette.fit: Close and built on the bodice; the full skirt stands free of the leg on its petticoat.
silhouette.proportion: Waist to hip about 1 to 1.6; hem 30 to 40 cm above the floor; jacket length to the top of the hip.
rules: Pinch the jacket at the waist and flare it over the hip into a padded basque.
Pleat or gather the skirt at the waist so that it opens in a bell.
Keep the neckline and the collar small, so that the waist leads.
Pair a full skirt with a narrow bodice, and a pencil skirt with a short, wide jacket.

fabrics.rule: Choose a cloth with body that holds a pleat and a bell. Use fine wool for day, silk taffeta and satin for evening, with tulle and canvas inside.

methods: knife and box pleats at the waist
tulle petticoat in three or more layers
construction.closures: Covered buttons down the front of the jacket; hooks and a side zip on the skirt, hidden under a placket.
construction.details: A round collar or a shawl collar, a padded basque on the jacket, and a self belt or none. Gloves and a small hat finish the look.

surface.pattern: Plain cloth for day in one colour; for evening, embroidery and beads on the bodice or a scatter on the skirt.
surface.gloss: Wool at 2–5 GU for day; satin and taffeta at 30–60 GU for evening.
surface.wear: The style wants a new, pressed piece; the couture house repairs and re-presses it, and a worn piece loses its line.

palette.strategy: Day dress in neutral wool, cream and black; evening dress in one deep colour or in pale silk.

processes: haute couture to the measure of the client
making.scale: Haute couture: each piece made to measure in the house, with three or more fittings; licensed patterns and copies for department stores.
making.signs: Hand-sewn hems and seams, an inner corselet and petticoat, and a pressed pleat that falls the same each time.

pieces.form: Short jacket with a pinched waist and a padded basque
Calf-length pleated skirt that opens in a bell
Strapless boned bodice with a full skirt over tulle
Day dress with a fitted bodice and a full skirt
Small round-collar blouse under the jacket

emotion.target_response: A sense of plenty and grace after years of shortage: the viewer sees the waist, the swing of the skirt and the hand work.

use_cases: a period costume brief for a 1950s film
a couture-inspired bridal or evening line
a fashion image prompt for a 1950s look
a museum label or study note on post-war dress
avoid_when: the brief is sportswear or casual dress
the brief wants comfort and stretch
the brief is a 1960s youth look

modifiers.how: Drop the boning and the petticoat, cut silk on the bias, and keep the small waist.
Raise the hem above the knee, straighten the line, and keep the neat tailoring.

sources.title: Victoria and Albert Museum: Christian Dior

ornament_level.note: Day suits are plain; evening gowns carry embroidery on the bodice.
